tierReason: Adds project data, new Prisma tables and new API endpoints, plus the offline sync layer

findings.text: queue.ts ~146-155 + routes.ts ~130 + ProjectsProvider.tsx ~134: an update is merged into a create whose response was lost (network after server stored it); the resent create returns the existing project unchanged and onApplied overwrites the local rename, so an offline rename is silently lost (R19, R25).

apps/mobile/src/app/(app)/projects/index.tsx: the project list never calls refresh() when shown (no useFocusEffect), so R17 'refresh whenever the project list is shown' isn't met; another member's delete/rename stays stale until foreground/reconnect.

apps/api/src/projects/routes.ts: no GET /projects/:id, so GET on a project falls to the generic notFoundHandler ('Not found.') while PATCH/DELETE say 'Project not found.'; AC10 asks reading, changing and deleting to give the same 404 body, and reading is untested.

apps/mobile/src/sync/queue.test.ts ~215 and ~237: AC26 test only checks onRejected + empty queue, not that the local copy shows the server's version / project removed on 404 and the notice is shown (ProjectsProvider logic untested); AC27 test never shows the change is sent after the same person signs in again.

queue.ts persist ~111 / load ~99: one rejected setJSON leaves the writes chain rejected forever, and a rejected first getJSON is cached in loading forever, so the queue stops working for the session; chain from writes.catch and reset loading on failure.
ProjectsProvider.tsx create ~319-330 (and update/remove): commit runs before queue.enqueue; if enqueue throws, the project is shown and cached but never queued, then vanishes at next refresh.
routes.ts ~105: GET /projects orderBy name has no tie-breaker; same-named projects can swap order between refreshes; add projectId asc.
store.test.ts ~36: 'a project missing from the server list is gone' calls applyOverlay([A], []) and expects [A]; it cannot fail, so AC19's 'refresh without B removes B' isn't really tested.
Repo root has no .gitignore; root node_modules/ shows as untracked and a git add -A would pick it up.

Sensitive: queue.ts runPass / ProjectsProvider flushInner: the queue never checks its ownerId against the signed-in user before sending; if setOwner fails or a flush queued before sign-in runs after it, user A's queued create could be sent with user B's token. Narrow window; fix by passing expected owner to flush or checking genRef before queue.flush().

Sensitive: queue.ts isPermanentRejection: 400 invalid_json/bad_request and 413 aren't permanent, and malformed persisted changes throw a TypeError treated as network; either one blocks the queue head forever. Treat all 4xx except 401/408/429 as permanent; validate persisted changes on load.
Sensitive: a delete resent after a lost reply gets 404 and shows 'couldn't be saved' though it worked; treat 404 on delete as success without a notice.
Sensitive: routes.ts requireOwner reads the role outside the write; once #5 adds role changes, a demoted Owner could still write in between. Before #5, put the owner condition in the write's where.
Sensitive: deleting a user leaves their projects with no members (reachable by nobody, ids 409 forever); handle when account deletion is built.
Sensitive: projects migration has no down script; additive only; undo by dropping ProjectMember, Project, ProjectRole, Currency; note in release notes.
Sensitive: GET /projects has no paging; out of scope by spec; record as a known limit.

Round 2: rejectedNotice is drawn only on Home with a current project; a 404 rejection on the current project clears currentProjectId, Home redirects to /projects which never shows it, and the stale notice later appears on an unrelated project (R26/AC26). Show it on the list too or in a shared (app) banner; clear on show/switch.

Round 2: outcomes.test.ts AC26 403 test asserts restoreFromServer([A,B],[]) equals [A,B], true regardless; the only thing restoring the server version is ProjectsProvider wiring (needsRefresh then refreshInner after flush), untested. Extract flush/apply/refresh into a plain function and test that after a 403 the list holds the server value; also that onSignedOut reaches handleNotSignedIn (AC27).
Round 2: edit.tsx delete sets deleting before an un-awaited remove(); if enqueue fails the screen renders null forever. Catch, reset deleting, show errors.generic.
Round 2: a refresh failing with 5xx silently sets status ready; list shows no error or retry.
Round 2: a change with no senders or a permanent 5xx stops the queue forever; consider a cap or way out.
Round 2: create sender sends one editedAt (latest) for all fields of a merged create; harmless now, not exactly per-field.
Round 2: AC22 has no test pinning the missing-sender type error (e.g. @ts-expect-error); AC16 language-independence is by design.
Round 2: new deps (async-storage, netinfo, expo-crypto, vitest) — approved in the plan by the user; retryProfile touches session handling, looks correct.

Round 3: edit.tsx 233-244 + ProjectsProvider update 313-333 + ProjectForm: the form submits all fields and update() diffs against the current cache, which a refresh may have changed while the form was open; a description-only save then queues the stale name with a fresh editedAt and reverts another device's newer rename (breaks R13). Diff against the form's initial values.
Round 3: AC16 'both app languages' not tested; formatMoney takes no language by design.
Round 3: AC19 removal only tested on applyOverlay; add a syncCycle refresh test where cache [A,B], server [A] leaves [A].
Round 3: syncCycle commits listProjects and create/patch replies to the cache without isProject checks; one malformed entry makes loadProjectCache discard the whole cache next launch (R18).
Round 3: outcomes.ts names the rejected notice after change.data.name (the rejected new name), not the project's known name.
Round 3: a non-network list refresh failure (5xx) shows no message.
Round 3: scope notes: retryProfile on foreground changes auth behaviour (state in PR); home greeting removed leaving home.welcome unused; root .gitignore and roadmap edits.
Round 3: spec R28 wipes the remembered project on sign-out, so R29/AC29 'opens the project used last' only happens after a 401, not a normal sign-out and sign-in; clarify AC29's by-hand step.
